proof:
Source: step 6(c) of the parent proof.
1. Let v ∈ tangentSpace N x. By definition there is γ : ℝ → ℝ^P with γ((−1, 1)) ⊆ N, γ(0) = x and γ′(0) = v (HasDerivAt γ v 0). The C¹ property of γ on (−1, 1) is not needed.
2. γ is continuous at 0 because it is differentiable there. Since γ(0) = x ∈ O and O is open, γ(s) ∈ O for all s in a neighbourhood of 0. Also (−1, 1) is a neighbourhood of 0. Hence for all s near 0, γ(s) ∈ N ∩ O and π(γ(s)) = γ(s). So π∘γ and γ agree on a neighbourhood of 0.
3. Chain rule: π is differentiable at γ(0) = x and γ has derivative v at 0, so π∘γ has derivative Dπ(x)v at 0 (Mathlib HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt).
4. By step 2, γ also has derivative Dπ(x)v at 0 (Mathlib HasDerivAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq). Derivatives are unique (HasDerivAt.unique), so Dπ(x)v = γ′(0) = v. ∎
key_steps: Take γ with γ((−1,1)) ⊆ N, γ(0) = x and γ′(0) = v.
Continuity of γ at 0 and openness of O give π∘γ = γ near 0.
The chain rule gives (π∘γ)′(0) = Dπ(x)v, and uniqueness of derivatives gives Dπ(x)v = v.
